overview: Duolingo is the world's leading mobile learning platform, offering language learning in 40+ languages alongside Math, Music, and Chess through a gamified, freemium app. As of Q2 2026 the company had 58.7 million daily active users (DAUs), 140.6 million monthly active users (MAUs), and 12.7 million paid subscribers, building on FY2025's first billion-dollar revenue year ($1.037B). The company remains in its self-declared 2026 'investment year,' deliberately prioritizing DAU growth and product quality over near-term monetization — though Q2 2026 results showed this trade-off improving on the margin side (EBITDA margin guidance raised) even as bookings growth continues to lag DAU growth sharply.

business_model.summary: Freemium model with the large majority of revenue from subscriptions, supplemented by advertising, the Duolingo English Test, and in-app purchases. Q2 2026 revenue was $298.5M (+18% YoY, beat consensus), while bookings grew only +8% YoY to $289.1M — a widening gap versus 23% DAU growth that is now the central market debate. Gross margin came in at 72.6% (above the ~71% guide) thanks to a dramatic AI cost reduction: Video Call inference cost fell from ~$0.30 to under $0.01 per call after switching from GPT-4 to an in-house/open-source model. FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to ~26.5% (from ~25% at the start of the year) on the back of these AI cost efficiencies, even as the top-line growth/monetization trade-off persists. In a major structural change announced around the Q2 print and accelerating into September 2026, Duolingo is sunsetting the premium Max tier and folding its AI features (Video Call, Roleplay, Explain My Answer) into the base Super subscription, betting that AI cost collapse makes premium-tier price segmentation unnecessary.

revenue_streams.name: Subscriptions (Super, formerly Super + Max)
revenue_streams.trend: growing but decelerating; tier consolidation into Super underway

business_model.customer_type: B2C (individual learners globally), with institutional use via Duolingo for Schools (COPPA/FERPA compliant) and B2B via Duolingo English Test accepted at 6,100+ programs
business_model.geographic_mix: North and Latin America ~55%, Europe/Middle East/Africa ~32%, Asia-Pacific ~13% (based on IAP revenue data); Asia remains the fastest-growing region, with continued performance-marketing and influencer investment in China and broader Asia through Q2 2026

main_competitors: PolyChat and other AI-native language apps
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in language learning apps by virtually every metric. FY2025 revenue of $1.037B dwarfs Babbel's ~$270M. #1 grossing app in Education on both Google Play and Apple App Store. Most downloaded language app globally with an order-of-magnitude DAU lead over nearest app competitors. Over 6,100 educational institutions accept Duolingo English Test.

moat_factors.description: Over 10 million users maintain streaks of 1+ years. Daily check-in habit makes Duolingo uniquely sticky vs. passive AI chatbots. Q2 2026 current-user retention reached an all-time high, up roughly 1 percentage point YoY, reinforcing the durability of these mechanics even as monetization lags.

Iconic owl mascot and 'unhinged' social media strategy make Duolingo one of the most recognized edtech brands globally. Organic word-of-mouth remains the primary user acquisition channel, evidenced by DAU growth (23% in Q2 2026) continuing to accelerate even as paid marketing spend is not scaling proportionally.

moat_factors.factor: Data flywheel and AI cost/content advantage
moat_factors.description: Billions of learning sessions generate proprietary data enabling personalized AI instruction. Beyond content velocity (20,500+ course units/quarter run-rate), the company has now demonstrated a proprietary AI cost advantage: migrating Video Call inference from GPT-4 to an in-house/open-source model cut per-call cost from ~$0.30 to under $0.01 (a ~97% reduction), which is both a margin lever and a reason management felt comfortable collapsing the Max/Super price tiers.

Robust free experience attracts 140.6M MAUs (Q2 2026, +10% YoY), creating an enormous top-of-funnel that converts to paid (12.7M subscribers). This scale is structurally difficult for competitors to replicate.
Expansion into Chess, Math, and Music continues to position Duolingo as a broader daily learning platform, not just a language app.

weaknesses: Bookings growth structurally lagging DAU growth: Q2 2026 bookings grew just +8% YoY versus 23% DAU growth — the widest growth gap disclosed to date, and the reason the stock sold off ~10-12% despite an EPS/revenue beat

Max tier being actively sunset (new subscribers no longer offered Max as of September 2026), confirming the ARPU-cannibalization risk flagged earlier in 2026 has become deliberate strategy rather than a rumored test — near-term revenue-per-subscriber will compress as ~10% of the paid base (former Max users, paying ~2x Super price) rolls onto standard Super pricing
Testing a lower-priced 'Super Lite' tier, which could further pressure blended ARPU even as it aids conversion
Dependency on Apple and Google app stores for distribution and payments (15-30% platform take rates)
Effectiveness ceiling debate: research suggests typical users plateau at A2-B1 (elementary/lower-intermediate), limiting retention of advanced learners
Analyst sentiment has cooled to consensus 'Hold' despite raised EBITDA guidance, reflecting persistent skepticism that DAU growth will convert to bookings growth on the timeline management implies

growth_drivers: AI cost collapse enabling tier simplification: Video Call cost per session fell ~97% (from ~$0.30 to under $0.01) after moving off GPT-4 to an in-house/open-source model, funding the Max-to-Super feature consolidation while still allowing FY2026 EBITDA margin guidance to be raised to ~26.5%
AI-accelerated content creation continuing at a run-rate near 20,000+ course units per quarter, enabling deeper courses and faster expansion of Chess, Math, and Music

Speaking and conversation features (Video Call, Spoken Tokens, Speaking Adventures) now being pushed into the mass-market Super tier rather than gated behind premium Max pricing, which should broaden usage and could accelerate the free-to-paid conversion funnel even if near-term ARPU is diluted

Record user engagement: Q2 2026 current-user retention hit an all-time high (+~1pp YoY), suggesting the 2026 investment-year strategy is working on the engagement side even where monetization has not yet followed
International expansion, particularly Asia: continued performance-marketing and influencer investment in China and broader Asia through Q2 2026
Duolingo English Test (DET) growth: accepted at 6,100+ institutions including 24 of the top 25 U.S. undergraduate programs by international enrollment

100M DAU medium-term target (CEO has referenced 2028): 58.7M DAUs as of Q2 2026, with management explicitly reiterating that 'users don't monetize immediately' but should convert to bookings growth over time

$400M share buyback program (no expiration): $72M cumulatively repurchased (~700,000 shares) through Q2 2026, including ~$44M repurchased in Q2 alone, providing a valuation floor and offsetting SBC dilution

business.risk: Bookings-to-DAU growth gap widening, not narrowing
business.description: Q2 2026 bookings grew +8% YoY vs. +23% DAU growth — a wider gap than the Q1 2026 pattern (14% bookings vs. 21% DAU). The core bull thesis (DAU growth eventually converts to bookings) has not yet shown evidence of inflecting after two consecutive quarters; management's own language ('it's going to take some time') concedes the timeline is uncertain.

business.risk: Max tier sunset creates near-term ARPU/revenue-mix risk
business.description: As of September 2026, new subscribers can no longer sign up for the ~2x-priced Max tier; its AI features have been folded into standard Super. Existing Max subscribers (~10% of paid base) will migrate to lower-priced Super over time, mechanically compressing revenue per subscriber even if total subscriber count and engagement improve. Whether the lower price point drives enough incremental conversion to offset the per-user revenue cut is unproven.

ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and AI-native language apps offer free or low-cost conversational practice. Studies suggest Duolingo users plateau at A2-B1, opening a gap AI tutors can fill. Duolingo's own aggressive AI cost-cutting (GPT-4 to in-house models) shows how quickly conversational AI commoditizes — a dynamic that could just as easily benefit standalone AI competitors.
Reliance on Apple and Google app stores for distribution and in-app purchase processing (15-30% take rates). Subject to platform policy changes.

financial.description: Full-year 2026 guidance still calls for only 10-12% bookings growth against mid-to-high-teens revenue growth and 20%+ DAU growth. If this gap persists into FY2027 rather than closing, it directly threatens both the historical bookings-based growth-rate assumptions in valuation models and the medium-term monetization thesis behind the 100M DAU target.

financial.risk: Gross margin trajectory now more favorable, but tier-mix dependent
financial.description: Q2 2026 gross margin of 72.6% beat the ~71% guide on AI cost efficiencies, a reversal of the prior narrative of structural margin erosion from AI costs. However, Q3 2026 gross margin is guided back down to ~71%, and the durability of the AI cost advantage (and its interaction with the Max-to-Super mix shift) is not yet a multi-quarter track record.
Over 50% of bookings from outside the US. USD strength creates a headwind to reported bookings and revenue.

financial.risk: SBC dilution, partially offset by buybacks
financial.description: Stock-based compensation remains elevated as a percent of revenue. The $400M buyback program has repurchased $72M (~700,000 shares) cumulatively through Q2 2026, providing only partial offset to gross dilution.

regulatory.description: Collects voice, biometric, and behavioral data from hundreds of millions of users including children. GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, and FERPA compliance obligations. Emerging AI regulations (EU AI Act) may impose restrictions on AI-generated educational content and data used for model training.
Continued investment in Chinese user acquisition is subject to unpredictable regulatory approvals, content restrictions, and data localization requirements.

EU Digital Markets Act and US regulatory action on Apple/Google could alter distribution economics, potentially improving Duolingo's margin (lower take rates) or disrupting existing revenue recognition patterns.

macro.description: Premium subscriptions are discretionary but low-ticket, and now more accessible with Max sunset and a lower-priced 'Super Lite' tier being tested. Education is relatively recession-resistant, and Duolingo's free tier provides a buffer.

macro.risk: Valuation still requires the DAU-to-bookings thesis to play out
macro.description: At ~$142/share (September 2026) and a market cap in the ~$6.5-7B range, DUOL trades well above its early-2026 lows (~$88) but analyst consensus has settled at 'Hold' (avg. target ~$134, though recent upgrades from Evercore ISI to $210 and DA Davidson to $175 show a wide dispersion of views). The stock's recovery from its 2026 lows already prices in some monetization re-acceleration that has not yet shown up in reported bookings growth.

execution.description: Sunsetting Max and folding its features into Super is a significant, fast-moving product and pricing change executed mid-year, on top of the already-announced 2026 strategic pivot to user growth. Missteps in migrating existing Max subscribers, or a failure of the lower blended price point to drive proportionally higher volume, would compound the existing bookings deceleration.

execution.risk: Strategic pivot still unproven on monetization
execution.description: Two consecutive quarters (Q1 and Q2 2026) have shown DAU growth significantly outpacing bookings growth, with the gap widening in Q2. Management continues to ask investors for patience ('users don't monetize immediately'), but the market's negative reaction to Q2 results (stock down ~10-12% despite a beat) shows patience is limited. As of Q2 2026 this remains the single largest swing factor for the stock.

CEO Luis von Ahn liquidated his entire directly-held Class A common stock position (28,292 shares, ~$4.3M) on September 16, 2026, under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted June 2, 2026. He retains ~3.4 million Class B/derivative securities, so this is not a meaningful reduction in economic alignment, but is worth monitoring as part of the broader insider-activity picture.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Online language learning market valued at ~$22B in 2026, projected to reach $94B by 2035 (18% CAGR per Business Research Insights). AI integration is the dominant industry trend, both as a threat (free AI tutors) and enabler (personalized, conversational learning at scale). Duolingo's Q2 2026 disclosure of a ~97% AI inference cost reduction demonstrates the pace at which AI unit economics are improving industry-wide, cutting both ways: it lowers Duolingo's costs but also lowers the barrier for new AI-native entrants.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low cyclicality. Education is resilient, and Duolingo's subscription price points are low relative to disposable income. Free tier with ads provides a fully functional product that buffers churn in downturns.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity. Growth stock valuation is sensitive to rates and growth-narrative sentiment — the stock fell from a $544 peak (May 2025) to a low of ~$88 (early 2026), then recovered to the ~$142 range by September 2026 on the back of the AI-cost-efficiency narrative and raised EBITDA guidance, even though bookings growth has not re-accelerated.
key_input_costs: Generative AI inference costs (now shifting toward in-house/open-source models from third-party APIs, delivering a large cost reduction)
Content creation (AI-assisted, but still requires editorial oversight)

recent_developments.event: CEO Luis von Ahn sold his entire directly-held Class A common stock position (28,292 shares, ~$4.3M) under a pre-planned Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted June 2, 2026. He retains ~3.4M Class B/derivative securities; not viewed as a signal of reduced conviction given the pre-planned, non-discretionary nature of the sale.

Reporting confirmed Duolingo is actively sunsetting the premium Max subscription tier: new subscribers as of mid-September 2026 no longer see Max as a sign-up option on iOS (current paid tiers: Lite $35.99/yr, Super Individual $16.99/mo or $119.99/yr, Super Family $143.99/yr). Max's AI features (Video Call, Roleplay, Explain My Answer) have been folded into the base Super tier, made economically feasible by a ~97% reduction in AI inference costs (Video Call cost fell from ~$0.30 to under $0.01/call after moving off GPT-4 to an in-house/open-source model).

Stock rallied roughly 14-22% over the trailing month/quarter into mid-September, aided by Duolingo's presentation at Citi's 2026 Global TMT Conference spotlighting AI tools, and by sell-side upgrades: Evercore ISI upgraded to Outperform, more than doubling its price target to $210 (from $105); DA Davidson raised its target to $175 (from $160, Buy rating). Stock traded around $142-147 as of September 20, 2026, still down ~14% YTD and ~46% over the trailing year.

Q2 2026 earnings reported. Revenue $298.5M (+18% YoY, beat ~$295.4-295.6M consensus). Bookings $289.1M (+8% YoY) — a sharp deceleration and the widest gap yet versus 23% DAU growth. Adjusted EPS $0.66 (beat $0.58-0.61 consensus, ~14% surprise). Net income $33.2M (11.1% margin) vs. $44.8M (17.8% margin) in Q2 2025. Gross margin 72.6% (beat ~71% guide) on AI cost efficiencies. DAUs 58.7M (+23% YoY, accelerating from Q1's +21%). MAUs 140.6M (+10% YoY). Paid subscribers 12.7M (+17% YoY). FCF $79M for the quarter. Stock fell ~10-12% in the following session(s) despite the beat, as investors focused on the widening bookings/DAU growth gap and cautious Q3 guidance.

Full-year 2026 guidance: bookings growth maintained at 10-12%, revenue growth maintained at 15-18% (~$1.21B), but Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to ~26.5% (from ~25% at the start of the year and ~25.7% as of Q1 2026), driven by the AI cost-efficiency gains. Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guided to ~$320M. Full-year FCF guided to over $375M (up from >$350M prior guide). Q3 2026 guidance: bookings ~$307M (+9% YoY), revenue ~$302M (+11% YoY), gross margin ~71%, Adjusted EBITDA ~$76M (~25.2% margin).

Share buyback update: Duolingo repurchased ~$44M of stock in Q2 2026 alone, bringing cumulative repurchases under the $400M authorization to $72M (~700,000 shares) since the program's February 2026 launch.

CEO Luis von Ahn on the bookings/DAU gap: 'Users don't monetize immediately... we expect higher DAUs will imply higher revenue, but it's going to take some time.' Management also disclosed testing of a lower-priced 'Super Lite' tier and continued build-out of Math and Music, alongside stepped-up performance marketing and influencer partnerships in Asia.
DUOL stock fell 9.24% on June 25, 2026, before a subsequent ~20% monthly recovery into late June driven by a re-rating after the Q1 2026 beat; stock traded near $120-121 as of June 26-27, 2026.

Q1 2026 earnings reported. Revenue $292M (+27% YoY, beat guide), Bookings $308.5M (+14% YoY), Adj. EBITDA $83.4M (28.6% margin, beat), Gross margin 73.0% (+190bps YoY). DAUs 56.5M (+21% YoY), Paid subscribers 12.5M (+21% YoY). Stock dropped 13.9% on Q2 bookings guidance miss. Full-year guidance maintained at $1.205B revenue and $1.28B bookings; Adj. EBITDA raised to $310M.

Q4 and FY2025 earnings reported. Revenue $1.037B (+39% YoY), Bookings $1.158B (+33% YoY), Adj. EBITDA margin 29.5%, FCF $360.4M. FY2026 guidance issued well below analyst consensus, and stock fell 22.5% to an intraday low of $91.61.
Board authorized $400M share repurchase program with no expiration date — Duolingo's first capital return program. As of Q2 2026, $72M (~700,000 shares) has been repurchased cumulatively.
New CFO Gillian Munson (former Vimeo CFO, ex-Duolingo Audit Committee Chair) officially started. Matt Skaruppa moved to advisory role.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Luis von Ahn on the bookings/DAU disconnect (Q2 2026 call): 'Users don't monetize immediately... we expect higher DAUs will imply higher revenue, but it's going to take some time.' On the Max tier: 'Another possibility, truthfully, is that we may actually sunset Max' — subsequently confirmed by September 2026 as new subscribers can no longer select Max, with its AI features folded into Super. On AI cost efficiency: management highlighted the ~97% reduction in Video Call inference cost (from ~$0.30 to under $0.01/call) after migrating off GPT-4 to an in-house/open-source model, framed as both a margin driver and the enabler of the Max-to-Super consolidation. Management also flagged testing of a lower-priced 'Super Lite' tier and continued investment in Math, Music, and Asia-focused performance marketing.

bull_case: AI cost collapse is a genuine structural advantage, not just a one-time saving: cutting Video Call inference cost by ~97% funded both a full-year EBITDA margin guidance raise (to 26.5%) and the confidence to simplify pricing (Max sunset) — evidence Duolingo's proprietary data/AI infrastructure moat is translating into real unit economics, not just marketing.

DAU growth is accelerating, not decelerating: Q2 2026's +23% YoY DAU growth (up from +21% in Q1) is the strongest read yet on the 2026 'investment year' strategy working on the engagement side, with current-user retention at an all-time high. If bookings simply lag DAU growth with a delay (as management argues) rather than never converting, FY2027 bookings growth could re-accelerate off a larger, stickier user base.

Max-to-Super consolidation could expand the paid funnel: folding premium AI features into the mass-market Super tier, alongside a lower-priced 'Super Lite' test, may materially lower the price barrier to premium conversion, an offensive move rather than a defensive one, particularly if AI feature usage drives higher retention across a much larger subscriber base.

Balance sheet strength and active capital return: no debt, strong FCF (guided >$375M for FY2026, above the >$350M prior guide), and an active $400M buyback program ($72M deployed through Q2 2026) provide downside protection and an offset to dilution.

Renewed sell-side conviction: Evercore ISI's upgrade to Outperform with a $210 target (more than doubling its prior target) and DA Davidson's raise to $175 signal that at least some analysts view the AI-cost-efficiency story as underappreciated after the stock's ~46% one-year decline; the stock has rallied ~14-22% over the trailing month/quarter into September 2026.
bear_case: The core monetization thesis has now failed to show up for two straight quarters, and the gap is widening: Q2 2026 bookings grew +8% YoY against +23% DAU growth — worse than Q1's 14%-vs-21% gap, not better. Management's 'it's going to take some time' is an increasingly strained explanation the longer bookings growth stays in single digits while DAU growth accelerates.

Max tier sunset is a real, current-quarter revenue headwind, not a hypothetical risk: ~10% of the paid base priced at roughly 2x Super now migrates to lower pricing. The bet that volume gains offset the per-subscriber ARPU cut, plus a newly-tested lower-priced 'Super Lite' tier, adds further near-term downward pressure on blended revenue per subscriber during an already bookings-challenged year.

Market has already re-rated the stock up ~14-22% over the past month/quarter on an EBITDA-margin and AI-cost story, while bookings growth guidance for Q3 (+9%) and the full year (10-12%) remains unchanged and weak — leaving the stock vulnerable to disappointment if Q3 results don't show the bookings inflection bulls are underwriting.

AI substitution risk cuts both ways: the same open-source/in-house model shift that slashed Duolingo's own AI costs by ~97% lowers the barrier for well-funded AI-native competitors (or Google/OpenAI-embedded language tools) to offer comparable conversational practice free or near-free, eroding the pricing rationale for Super/paid tiers altogether.

Analyst consensus remains lukewarm (Hold, average target ~$134, some individual targets as low as ~$99) despite the recent rally and raised EBITDA guidance, reflecting persistent institutional skepticism about the durability of the DAU-to-bookings conversion story following a second consecutive quarter of stock decline on an earnings beat.
